sentences.text: The wife, the son, the daughter, the mother and the father of the deceased Narasimhappa alias K.N.Narasimhamurthy filed an application claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- urging a ground that the deceased Narasimhappa died in a road traffic accident that occurred on 20.06.2017.

The Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Sira which dealt with the matter as MVC No.1165/2017 on 20.12.2019 rendered an order holding that the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.13,30,000/- as compensation.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Sira
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Projecting that they are entitled for enhanced sum
, the claimants are before this Court through this appeal.

3. Arguing the matter, learned counsel Sri.Shreyas.N for appellants contends that the deceased Narasimhappa (hereinafter be referred to as the 'deceased' for brevity) by NC: 2024:KHC:37469 selling coconuts and through agriculture was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
However, the Tribunal assessed and took the notional income of the deceased as Rs.8,000/- per month, which is unjustifiable.

Learned counsel contends that the accident occurred in the year 2017 and for the relevant period, the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is taking notional income as Rs.11,000/- per month and atleast the said figure should have been considered by the Tribunal.

Learned counsel further submits that though the claimants are the wife, children and parents of the deceased, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/- only towards loss of consortium, which is unjustifiable.
Learned counsel ultimately seeks for enhancement of compensation.
4. On the other hand, Sri.Mallikarjun Reddy representing respondent No.2 Insurance Company contends that the amount awarded as compensation is justifiable.
However, learned counsel did not raise any objection to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.11,000/- per month.

Also the request made in this regard is justifiable.
NC: 2024:KHC:37469 5.
Admittedly, the deceased died at the age of 41 years.

Thus, 25% of the earnings of the deceased are required to be added towards future prospects as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Also as the dependents are five in number, 1/4th of the earnings are required to be deducted towards the personal and living expenses which the deceased would have incurred for himself had he been alive.

Also the appropriate multiplier to be applied as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reported in AIR 2009 SC 3104 is '14'.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reported in AIR 2009 SC 3104
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, with the said parameters, the loss of dependency is as under:
Amount Description In Rs.
 Notional monthly income 11,000-00  Annual Income (11,000X12) 1,32,000-00  Add 25% towards future  1,65,000-00  prospects (Rs.1,32,000/- + 25%)
 Deduct 1/4th towards personal  1,23,750-00 Puttanarasamma vs Manju K on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85016488/
3  and living expenses  Applying appropriate multiplier  17,32,500-00  '14'
6.
Thus the appellants are entitled to a sum of Rs.17,32,500/- under the head loss of dependency.

Together NC: 2024:KHC:37469 with the said amount, the appellants are entitled to Rs.15,000/-
towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.
Appellant No.1 being the wife of the deceased is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium.
Appellant Nos.2 and 3 being the children of the deceased are entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards loss of parental consortium.
Appellant Nos.4 and 5 being the parents of the deceased are entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards loss of filial consortium.

Thus, the compensation which the appellants are entitled to under different heads is as under:
Amount Sl No.
Compensation
in Rs.

1 Loss of dependency 17,32,500-00 2 Funeral expenses 15,000-00 3 Loss of estate 15,000-00 4 Loss of spousal consortium 40,000-00 5 Loss of parental consortium 40,000-00 6 Loss of filial consortium 40,000-00 Total 18,82,500-00 7.
The Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.13,30,000/- only towards compensation.
However, the justifiable sum which the appellants are entitled to as NC: 2024:KHC:37469 compensation is Rs.18,82,500/-.

Thus, the appeal is disposed of with the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The compensation that is awarded by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sira, through orders in MVC No.1165/2017 dated 20.12.2019 is enhanced from Rs.13,30,000/- to Rs.18,82,500/-.
(iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
